newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to stop encouraging S.Africa investment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to stop encouraging S.Africa investment.

text.p: The Taiwan government will not continue to encourage investments in South Africa, which plans to switch diplomatic ties to Beijing from Taipei at the end of 1997, Taiwan's top economic policy planner said on Thursday.
"The government will not continue to encourage investments in South Africa," Chiang Ping-kun, chairman of the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development, told reporters.

"Without government encourgement, it will be hard (for private investments) to proceed there," Chiang said when asked whether a US$3 billion petrochemical project by Taiwan's Tuntex Distinct Corp in South Africa would continue.

Tuntex, one of the island's major business groups, said earlier on Thursday it would respect the government's wishes in deciding whether to continue its US$3 billion petrochemical project in South Africa.
South Africa announced on Wednesday it would drop diplomatic ties with Taipei in 1997 in favour of the island's arch rival in Beijing.
